transcript: Last night I attended Show/Boat: A River at NYU Skirball, a drastic reimagining of the seminal musical Show Boat. With this production being by Target Margin Theater with Under The Radar, I knew it would be interesting, and boy was it. I'm not familiar with the original, so I don't think I fully grasped the extent of this production's directorial choices. But based on the plot alone, it's understandable why putting up a classically staged production of Show Boat might not go over well for today's audiences. This production feels visually deconstructed and knowingly performative in a way that I believe is meant to highlight the questionable aspects of the source material and contextualize it within today's society. It felt a little uneven in terms of tone, which left me wondering exactly how I'm supposed to feel about the story, and I overall wish that the production had committed to some of the ideas a little more wholeheartedly. But the score, for the most part holds up decently and I was quite impressed by some of the singing and the relatively full-sounding orchestra, despite it being only six musicians. Show/Boat: A River is running at Skirball through January 26th. With that, another program for my collection.
